name: Granite State Eats: NH
subtitle: Ice Cream, Lobster & Pancakes
description:
New Hampshire's restaurants, from a dairy farm's own ice cream in the North Country to a lobster pound on the Seabrook harbor.

Granite State Eats is a free guide to eating in New Hampshire: 51 ice cream stands and creameries, 11 Seacoast lobster pounds and seafood shacks, and 8 pancake houses and diners we checked by hand, plus 3,221 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 187 towns, from Manchester and Portsmouth to the Lakes Region and the White Mountains. No account, no ads.

NEW HAMPSHIRE GUIDES
• Ice Cream Stands: dairy bars and creameries on Visit NH's 2026 Ice Cream Trail.
• Seacoast Seafood: lobster pounds and shacks from Seabrook to Portsmouth.
• Pancake Houses & Diners: sugar-house breakfasts with real maple syrup, and classic diners.
• Oldest Places: 3 restaurants with a checked founding year.
• James Beard Honors: 5 honored New Hampshire restaurants.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "ice cream", "lobster seabrook", "pancakes".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 article or Visit NH's own 2026 Ice Cream Trail. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested where cities publish official restaurant lists. New Hampshire's Department of Health and Human Services posts its inspection results on its own search and publishes none as data, so each place links that search, and the app shows no inspection results. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Granite State Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of New Hampshire, the Department of Health and Human Services or Visit NH), or with the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Granite State Eats is a free guide to restaurants in New Hampshire (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: ice cream stands, Seacoast lobster pounds and seafood shacks, and pancake houses and diners, 71 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 3,221 restaurants, cafés and bars in 187 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Ice Cream Stands (or Seacoast Seafood, Pancake Houses & Diners, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services' inspection search in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("ice cream", "lobster seabrook", "pancakes").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside New Hampshire (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on New Hampshire, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Granite State Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Granite State Eats: NH".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Granite State Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and Visit NH's 2026 Ice Cream Trail.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/new-hampshire-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers New Hampshire; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or award body.

Support: nick@eatsranked.com
